newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's May inflation seen under one percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's May inflation seen under one percent.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index should rise less than one percent in May, Banco de Mexico governor Miguel Mancera said on Wednesday.

"The inflationary trajectory has been as forecast, and thus, we can expect that in the present month the monthly increase in the general level of prices will fall to less than one percent," Mancera said.
He was speaking to journalists at a news conference called to defend the central bank's monetary policy.
Press reports on Wednesday suggested the central bank was running a loose monetary policy that could lead to inflationary pressures.
But Mancera said monetary policy was not loose and that declining inflation helped prove this.
In April the inflation rate was 1.08 percent, after reaching 1.24 percent in March.
